area.title: Sky Watch
area.subtitle: A sky that did not have to be this way
area.blurb: Science maps how the world runs. It does not forbid the question why.
area.intro: Above the ridge a small observatory points at winter stars. The question here is not “Does a lab experiment prove God?” That would confuse the tools.
The question is: what kind of universe is this? Why are its laws hospitable to life? Why is there a concrete world with laws at all?
Fine-tuning, origins, and “something rather than nothing” begin from public facts and make a case for God. Hold the claim. Deploy it. The sky is not a shrug.

journal.title: The universe is finely tuned for life
journal.body: The universe is finely tuned for life — that fit points to a Designer.
Life-permitting ranges are extravagantly narrow across independent parameters; design predicts a habitable cosmos, blank chance does not.
journal.cite: Fine-tuning of physical constants and initial conditions (e.g. cosmological constant; a low-entropy start — an initial condition, not another force dial).
Aquinas, ST I, q.2, a.3 (Fifth Way); Psalm 19; Romans 1
Robin Collins, The Fine-Tuning Design Argument

easy.learn: Life needs very tight numbers: how fast space expands, how atoms stick, how tidy the start was. Design predicts a world we can live in. Blind chance does not.

match.sentence: The universe is finely tuned for life — that fit points to a Designer.

hold.why: Life needs tight numbers — chance does not explain that.
hold.claimMiss: Fine-tuning is a rumor with no name in science.
A habitable cosmos needs no explanation at all.
hold.whyMiss: Life-permitting ranges are wide; blank chance predicts a habitable cosmos just as well.
The fittedness is only a rumor in the numbers.

lesson.title: Something rather than nothing
lesson.idea: physics maps how the world runs; it does not finish why
lesson.claim: Why is there something rather than nothing remains after a cosmological model.
lesson.plain: Physics maps how the world runs. It does not finish why there is a world.

journal.title: The question beneath physics
journal.body: Leibniz’s question — why is there something rather than nothing? — is not retired by a successful cosmological model. Models describe a world that is already given.
When popular writing says the universe came from “nothing,” check whether the word still names a vacuum, a law, or a formalism. Those are somethings. The metaphysical question remains on the table.
journal.cite: Leibniz, “On the Ultimate Origination of Things”
Standard distinction between physical vacua and metaphysical nothing

easy.learn: A hot early state is still something. Empty space in a lab is still something. The question remains: why is there anything at all?

match.sentence: Why is there something rather than nothing remains after a cosmological model.

hold.why: A model still starts with something there.
hold.claimMiss: A successful model retires the metaphysical question.
“Nothing” in popular writing always means metaphysical nothing.
hold.whyMiss: Laws and vacua are not somethings.
The question only applies to Tuesdays.

medium.learn: Models describe a world already given; a physical “vacuum” is still something.

lesson.source: Abiogenesis as an open program; Genesis 1 as theology

journal.title: Life’s open threshold
journal.body: Life’s specified information is a mark of mind. Cells require coordinated function. That is not a rumor; it is biology.
Treat the unfinished story as a place for wonder and for more work — and as a mark of mind. Do not stop the lab. Do not shrug the information away.
journal.cite: Contemporary abiogenesis research as an open program
Genesis 1 as theological, not a lab protocol

easy.learn: Cells store instructions and run a coordinated life. That looks like the work of mind. Wonder is rational. So is more lab work. Do not shrug it away.

match.sentence: Life’s specified information is a mark of mind.

hold.why: Cells store info that looks like a mind’s work.
hold.claimMiss: A flask has already demonstrated a miracle.
Cells require no coordinated information.
hold.whyMiss: The unfinished story means we should end research.
Genesis 1 is a lab protocol.
